Analysis of Bus Operator Management App Event Flow

The dataset encompasses a total of 14,985 events recorded between November 27, 2025 and February 19, 2026. There are 109 unique event types within this aggregate data.

Findings

a) DOMINANT PATHWAYS

The top 5 transitions represent the most frequent consecutive actions taken by users:

  • viewed_hisab_page → viewed_hisab_page (1310 counts)
  • viewed_hisab_bus_detail → viewed_hisab_page (798 counts)
  • viewed_hisab_page → viewed_hisab_bus_detail (750 counts)
  • viewed_hisab_bus_detail → viewed_hisab_bus_detail (472 counts)
  • viewed_dashboard_page → viewed_hisab_page (326 counts)

These transitions indicate that users frequently navigate back to the "hisab" page, suggesting it is a central hub for further actions.

b) DEAD ENDS

There are no specific transitions leading to "error" or "failure" events identified in the top transitions. However, it is essential to monitor any transitions that may lead to such outcomes in future analyses.

c) UNEXPECTED JUMPS

Transitions between unrelated workflows were not explicitly identified in the top transitions. However, the frequent navigation between "hisab" pages and bus details suggests potential confusion or friction in the user experience.

d) LOOPING

Several events show transitions back into themselves, indicating repetition:

  • viewed_hisab_page → viewed_hisab_page (1310 counts)
  • viewed_hisab_bus_detail → viewed_hisab_bus_detail (472 counts)

This self-looping behavior may indicate that users are unsure how to proceed or are revisiting information multiple times.

In conclusion, while the data reveals strong pathways and some looping behaviors, further investigation into dead ends and unexpected jumps may provide deeper insights into user navigation and potential areas for improvement in the app's design.
